details:
VITAL is a mission-health memory for long-duration spaceflight. Crew health over months isn’t a dashboard problem but a continuity problem, so VITAL records health as an append-only event log. Nothing is overwritten; a correction appends a new linked event, and each astronaut’s events form a SHA-256 hash chain, making the timeline verifiable rather than merely trusted. Every alert cites the event IDs that produced it.

Between hardware and the record sit four layers: adapters that normalize each source into a canonical 21-metric schema, a message bus with a durable queue that survives restarts, time synchronization, and fusion. Fusion is the core idea. VITAL ignores population thresholds and instead builds a personal rolling baseline, requiring two independent sensors at high quality agreeing over time before escalating. One sensor raises a follow-up. A single reading escalates nothing.

Telemetry comes from the VITAL Patch, our ESP32 DevKit V1 prototype: MPU6050 motion and posture, DHT22 cabin air temperature and humidity, OLED feedback, buzzer and status LED, with on-device paced-breathing cues. It has no heart-rate sensor, so heart rate is simulated and labelled as such everywhere.

Built with TanStack Start, React 19, Vite, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Zod schemas as the source of truth, Dexie/IndexedDB, Zustand and Recharts; firmware in Arduino C++ prototyped in Wokwi; 3D model compressed with gltf-transform and rendered locally via model-viewer; 119 tests in Vitest. Fields map to concepts from NASA’s Life Sciences Portal, LSAH, HRP Standard Measures and LSDA, with no private or restricted human-subject data used or implied.

Code, tests, documentation and the synthetic demo dataset were written with substantial assistance from Anthropic’s Claude (Opus 5). Hardware, firmware, 3D model and product direction are the team’s own. No SI-generated images, audio or video, and no NASA branding anywhere.

The creative decision was treating uncertainty as a feature. VITAL is not a medical device and makes no diagnostic claims, so sensor gaps render as visible breaks instead of interpolated lines, absent self-reports stay absent, and the emergency screen states plainly that the prototype sends no messages — with a test that fails if that wording ever softens.
